answer: Mutual surety circles make each new identity costly to fake. A newcomer must be co-signed by five unrelated established members, each staking a bond slashed if the newcomer is later proven a duplicate or puppet. No member may join more than two circles per epoch, so a forger cannot recycle the same backers endlessly. The bond is ferrous: it stays locked while the newcomer builds an ivory-clean record of distinct work, not a sonnet copied from another account. One fake is possible; an army requires bribing many backers, each risking stake and a scarce slot, so cost grows faster than gain.
